pattern_description: Missing authorisation check before accessing resource
example_bad:
def get_user_data(user_id):
    return db.query(f'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id={user_id}')
why_bad: Any caller can read any user's data without an ownership or role check.
fix: Verify that request.user.id == user_id or that the user has an admin role before querying.

pattern_description: Route handler missing authentication middleware
why_bad: Unauthenticated users can access privileged endpoints.
fix: Add authentication and authorisation middleware: app.get('/admin/users', requireAuth, requireAdmin, handler).

pattern_description: No role check before sensitive operation
example_bad: public Response deleteUser(Long id) { userService.delete(id); return ok(); }
why_bad: Any authenticated user can delete any other user's account.
fix: Add @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") or manual role check before the delete.

pattern_description: IDOR — object looked up by user-controlled ID without ownership check
example_bad: func getDocument(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { id := r.URL.Query().Get("id"); doc := db.Find(id); json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(doc) }
why_bad: Attacker increments id to access other users' documents.
fix: After fetching doc, assert doc.OwnerID == currentUser.ID; return 403 otherwise.

pattern_description: Hardcoded secret or API key in source code
why_bad: Secrets committed to source control can be harvested by anyone with repo access or via git history.
fix: Use os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY') and store secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager.

pattern_description: Weak hashing algorithm (MD5 or SHA-1) for password or integrity check
why_bad: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for cryptographic purposes; rainbow tables exist for common passwords.
fix: Use bcrypt, argon2, or hashlib.sha256 with a per-user salt for passwords. Use SHA-256+ for integrity.

pattern_description: Storing password in plaintext or with weak encoding
why_bad: A database dump exposes all user passwords directly.
fix: Use bcrypt.hash(req.body.password, 12) before storing. Never store plaintext passwords.

pattern_description: Using ECB mode cipher or hardcoded IV
why_bad: ECB mode is deterministic — identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext, leaking patterns.
fix: Use AES/GCM/NoPadding with a random IV per encryption. Store IV alongside ciphertext.

pattern_description: String concatenation in SQL query construction
example_bad:
query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username="' + username + '"'
cursor.execute(query)
why_bad: Attacker sets username to " OR 1=1 -- to dump the entire table or bypass authentication.
fix: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = %s', (username,))

pattern_description: Unsanitised user input inserted into HTML (XSS)
why_bad: Attacker sets name to <script>stealCookies()</script> to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victim's browser.
fix: Use textContent instead of innerHTML, or sanitise with DOMPurify before insertion.

pattern_description: Shell command constructed from user input
why_bad: Attacker passes user_path as '. && rm -rf /' to execute arbitrary commands.
fix: subprocess.run(['ls', user_path], shell=False) — never use shell=True with user input.

pattern_description: JPQL/HQL query built by string concatenation
example_bad: String q = "FROM User WHERE name='" + name + "'"; session.createQuery(q).list();
why_bad: Classic SQL injection via ORM layer — bypasses prepared statement protections.
fix: session.createQuery("FROM User WHERE name = :name").setParameter("name", name).list();

pattern_description: fmt.Sprintf used to build SQL query
example_bad:
query := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = %s", userID)
db.Query(query)
why_bad: String interpolation in SQL is always injectable regardless of language.
fix: db.Query("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = $1", userID)

pattern_description: Debug mode enabled in production Flask/Django app
example_bad:
app.run(debug=True)
# or
DEBUG = True  # in settings.py
why_bad: Debug mode exposes an interactive debugger, full tracebacks, and config values to anyone who triggers an error.
fix: Set DEBUG = False in production. Use environment-based config: DEBUG = os.getenv('DEBUG', 'False') == 'True'.

pattern_description: CORS configured to allow all origins with credentials
why_bad: Allowing all origins with credentials enables cross-origin requests from any website with the user's cookies.
fix: Specify exact allowed origins: cors({ origin: 'https://yourdomain.com', credentials: true }).

pattern_description: Default or trivially guessable admin credentials
why_bad: Default credentials are the first thing attackers try and are widely published in exploit databases.
fix: Require credentials to be set via environment variables with no defaults. Validate on startup.

pattern_description: requirements.txt pins dependency to known-vulnerable version
why_bad: Old versions may have known CVEs. Pinning without review means vulnerabilities stay indefinitely.
fix: Regularly update dependencies. Use 'pip audit' or Dependabot to alert on CVEs.

pattern_description: package.json dependency with wildcard version allowing vulnerable ranges
why_bad: Wildcard ranges can resolve to versions with known prototype pollution or other CVEs.
fix: Pin exact versions and run 'npm audit'. Use Dependabot or Snyk to track CVE alerts.

pattern_description: Session token not invalidated on logout
why_bad: Server-side session is not explicitly invalidated; tokens in logs or browser history remain valid.
fix: Call session.clear() and regenerate the session ID. For JWTs, maintain a server-side blocklist.

pattern_description: Weak or trivially brute-forceable password validation
why_bad: 4-character passwords are brute-forceable in milliseconds. No complexity or breach-check enforced.
fix: Enforce min length ≥12, require mixed case + digit + symbol, check against HaveIBeenPwned API.

pattern_description: JWT verified without checking algorithm field
why_bad: If alg is not validated, an attacker can craft a token with alg:none to bypass signature verification.
fix: jwt.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: ['HS256'] }) — always pin the expected algorithm.

pattern_description: Downloaded file executed or imported without integrity verification
why_bad: Attacker who controls the URL or intercepts the request can serve malicious code that runs with full privileges.
fix: Verify a SHA-256 hash of the download against a known-good value before importing or executing.

pattern_description: eval() or Function() called on remotely-fetched string
example_bad:
const code = await fetch('/api/plugin').then(r => r.text());
eval(code);
why_bad: eval() on remote content is remote code execution. Any compromise of the API server executes attacker code.
fix: Never eval remote content. Use a sandboxed iframe or Web Worker with strict CSP instead.

pattern_description: User-supplied URL passed directly to requests.get or urllib
why_bad: Attacker passes http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data to read cloud instance metadata, or internal services.
fix: Validate the URL against an allowlist of safe schemes and hosts. Block private IP ranges (10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x).

pattern_description: HTTP client called with user-controlled URL without host validation
why_bad: SSRF allows attackers to probe internal network services or cloud metadata endpoints.
fix: Parse the URL, check host against an allowlist, and block RFC-1918 address ranges before making the request.

pattern_description: fetch() or axios called with unvalidated user-provided URL
why_bad: Attacker supplies an internal service URL to exfiltrate credentials or probe internal topology.
fix: Validate imageUrl against an allowlist of trusted domains. Use a proxy service that strips internal routing.

pattern_description: Using math/rand instead of crypto/rand for security tokens
why_bad: math/rand is seeded deterministically and predictable. An attacker can enumerate all possible tokens.
fix: import "crypto/rand"; use rand.Read() to generate cryptographically random bytes for tokens.

pattern_description: User input passed to eval() or exec()
why_bad: eval() executes arbitrary Python code — trivial remote code execution.
fix: Never call eval/exec on user input. Use ast.literal_eval for safe expression parsing of literals only.

pattern_description: File path traversal via user-controlled filename
why_bad: Attacker passes ../../etc/passwd to read arbitrary files on the server.
fix: Use os.path.realpath() and assert the resolved path starts with the intended base directory.
source_label: OWASP A01:2021 — Broken Access Control (Path Traversal)

pattern_description: Spring Security permits all requests by default
why_bad: All endpoints are publicly accessible; any future route added is unauthenticated by default.
fix: Use .anyRequest().authenticated() as the default and explicitly permit only public paths.

pattern_description: Template literal used to build SQL or NoSQL query
example_bad: const result = await db.query(`SELECT * FROM posts WHERE id = ${req.params.id}`);
why_bad: TypeScript does not sanitise template literal values — SQL injection is identical to plain JS.
fix: await db.query('SELECT * FROM posts WHERE id = $1', [req.params.id]);

pattern_description: Password compared with == instead of constant-time comparison
why_bad: Timing differences in string equality can leak password length or characters via timing attack.
fix: Use MessageDigest.isEqual() or a constant-time comparison function. Better: use BCrypt.checkpw().

pattern_description: Sensitive data logged in plaintext
why_bad: Passwords and tokens in log files can be read by anyone with log access or log aggregation tools.
fix: Never log passwords, tokens, or PII. Log only non-sensitive identifiers like user IDs.

pattern_description: Admin route guarded only by client-side check
why_bad: Client-side rendering checks are trivially bypassed by modifying the JWT or local state.
fix: Enforce admin checks server-side on every API call. The UI check is cosmetic only.

pattern_description: Pickle deserialisation of untrusted data
why_bad: Pickle can execute arbitrary code during deserialisation. Passing attacker-controlled bytes is full RCE.
fix: Never unpickle untrusted data. Use JSON, msgpack, or protobuf for external data interchange.

pattern_description: Exception details exposed to client in API response
example_bad:
except Exception as e:
    return jsonify({'error': str(e)}), 500
why_bad: Stack traces and internal paths in error responses help attackers map the system.
fix: Log the full exception server-side; return a generic error message to the client.

pattern_description: XML parsed from user input with external entity expansion enabled
example_bad:
from lxml import etree
tree = etree.parse(user_xml_file)
why_bad: XXE allows attackers to read local files or perform SSRF via XML entity declarations.
fix: etree.parse(f, etree.XMLParser(resolve_entities=False, no_network=True))

pattern_description: go.mod pinned to module version with known CVE
why_bad: jwt-go v3.x has CVE-2020-26160 (missing claim validation). Maintainer-abandoned.
fix: Replace with github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 which is the maintained fork with fixes.

pattern_description: Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoint
why_bad: Attacker can brute-force credentials with unlimited attempts.
fix: Use Flask-Limiter: @limiter.limit('5 per minute') on the login route.

pattern_description: RestTemplate or WebClient called with URL from request parameter
why_bad: SSRF allows the server to be used as a proxy to reach internal services or cloud metadata.
fix: Validate the URL host against an allowlist. Block 169.254.x.x, 10.x.x.x, and 192.168.x.x ranges.
